findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new FallbackLocaleList class (custom fallback ordering and ensure_loaded!) ships with no test in the diff exercising its [] or ensure_loaded! behavior. A regression in the fallback chain (e.g. SiteSetting.default_locale dropped from the list, or ensure_loaded! silently no-op'ing) leaves users seeing missing-translation keys instead of fallback text, with no test failing to catch it.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! duplicates the @loaded_locales membership-check logic that translate already performs inline, creating two parallel places that must agree on how 'loaded' is tracked. The next change to load_locale's caching (e.g. swapping @loaded_locales to a Set or adding a mutex) must be applied in both the translate guard and ensure_loaded! or the two paths diverge and one issues redundant loads or serves an unloaded locale.

[BUG] The new ensure_loaded! method and the FallbackLocaleList fallback-order logic in config/initializers/i18n.rb are added with zero test coverage in this diff. Evidence of absence: the diff contains no test-shaped files (no spec/, test/, *.spec.* entries), so the two behaviors this PR exists to deliver — per-locale fallback order [user locale, site locale, :en] and lazy preloading of fallback locales — have no regression guard; a change to FallbackLocaleList#[] or ensure_loaded! that drops :en or the site locale would ship silently, reintroducing MissingTranslationData errors in production.

[BUG] Fallback-locale preloading is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, so all non-controller I18n consumers (mailers, background jobs, serializers outside a request) never have their fallback locales loaded. A background job or mailer rendering with a user locale whose translations are incomplete (e.g. site default :en as fallback) hits I18n.t on an unloaded fallback locale; because I18n::Backend::Fallbacks consults fallbacks[locale] but nothing in these paths calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, the fallback translations are not loaded from the store and the mailer/job renders missing-translation strings instead of the English fallback the PR promises — the requirement 'fallbacks work server-side' is only satisfied for web requests.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] returns locale values of mixed type: I18n.locale is a symbol but SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym covers site, and any caller passing a string locale gets a string element back that I18n::Backend::Fallbacks must normalize. If any I18n call path passes a string locale (e.g. from a serialized job payload or a header-derived locale), the returned fallback list mixes String and Symbol entries; I18n's fallback chain keys translations by symbol, so the string entry produces a lookup on an unloaded/mismatched key rather than a hard failure — the next contributor extending this list inherits an untyped contract with no normalization step.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! mutates the shared @loaded_locales array without synchronization, on a method invoked per-request from set_locale across Puma threads. Two concurrent first requests for the same locale can both pass the include? check and both run load_locale, doubling locale-load work on cold start and racing on the array append; existing load_locale callers had the same shape, but this diff adds a new per-request entry point that widens the race window to every request until locales warm up.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! is defined on FallbackLocaleList but called as I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! from the controller with no type guarantee that I18n.fallbacks is still a FallbackLocaleList at that point. The controller now has a hard runtime dependency on an initializer-assigned singleton: if any test or boot path reassigns I18n.fallbacks (e.g. a spec stubbing fallbacks with a plain Hash or I18n::Locale::Fallbacks instance, which Rails' own config.i18n.fallbacks=true would produce), set_locale raises NoMethodError (undefined method 'ensure_loaded!') on every request, turning a misconfiguration into a site-wide 500.

[BUG] The initializer unconditionally enables I18n fallbacks in every environment, but the three deleted `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were only in production/profile/cloud66 — so development and test environments silently gain fallback-to-default behavior they never had. Tests that assert missing translations (I18n::MissingTranslation / I18n::ArgumentError on lookup miss) now silently resolve via the :en fallback and pass or fail differently, and developers no longer see missing-translation keys raised in dev, masking untranslated-locale regressions.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash while overriding #[], leaving every other Hash behavior (keys, each, has_key?, size) operating on an always-empty store. Any code (I18n internals, plugins, tests) that introspects I18n.fallbacks as a Hash — e.g. enumerating configured fallback chains or reading fallbacks[locale]= style writes — gets empty results or silently stores data that the overridden [] never returns; the next change to fallback configuration has to work around a Hash that is not a functioning Hash.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! duplicates the loaded-check pattern that translate (line 66) re-implements inline, creating two parallel bookkeeping sites for @loaded_locales. A future change to how loaded locales are tracked (e.g. moving to a Set, or invalidation on locale reload) must be made in both places; missing one yields stale-translation or double-load bugs that are hard to spot.

[ADVISORY] The new FallbackLocaleList class and its ensure_loaded! behavior have no test coverage in this diff, nor does the controller hook in application_controller.rb. A regression in the fallback chain ordering (e.g. dropping SiteSetting.default_locale) or in eager locale loading would silently change which translation text users see, with no failing test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! loads the fallback chain for I18n.locale, while translate_accelerator's translate loads config.locale — two separate sources of truth for the current locale. Wherever I18n.locale and I18n.config.locale diverge (e.g. code that sets I18n.locale directly without going through the site/user locale resolution that set_locale performs), the eager-load primes a different locale set than translate will actually demand, so the first lookup can still hit a cold load on the request path it was meant to protect.

[BUG] Fallback-locale loading is wired only into the web request lifecycle (ApplicationController#set_locale), so all non-request I18n contexts never load the fallback chain. Sidekiq jobs, mailers, and other background code that sets I18n.locale to a user's locale rely on the Fallbacks backend to resolve keys, but nothing calls ensure_loaded! there — the fallback locales (site default and :en) are absent from the accelerator's @loaded_locales and its store, so background-rendered emails and job-generated content emit raw translation keys instead of falling back to English, an inconsistency between web and background rendering that appears only in production paths.

[ADVISORY] The initializer applies FallbackLocaleList to every environment including test, changing what 'missing translation' means under test. Previously fallbacks existed only in production/profile via env config; now any spec asserting that a key is untranslated (or relying on I18n::MissingTranslation for an exotic locale) silently receives the English fallback instead, so the test suite goes green on incomplete locale coverage — a stand-in-guard effect where the test environment can no longer detect the exact defect this feature is meant to manage.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! mutates @loaded_locales via ||= and include? with no synchronization, adding a second unsynchronized writer to shared mutable state on a multithreaded hot path. Under a threaded server (Puma), the first concurrent requests can both see the locale as unloaded and race load_locale; the pre-existing pattern in translate had the same shape, but this diff adds a new entry point invoked unconditionally per request, widening the race window rather than fixing the structure.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! runs on every request even when the accelerator's translate path would lazily load what is needed, and there is no test in the diff covering ensure_loaded! or the custom fallback ordering. Every request pays the fallback-chain computation and three include? checks; more importantly, the nontrivial new logic in FallbackLocaleList#[] (user-locale → site-locale → :en ordering, uniq/compact) has no spec, so a regression that reorders or drops the site-locale tier ships silently.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash without ever calling super for [] or storing entries, faking a lookup table with an open method. Any I18n or plugin code that treats I18n.fallbacks as a real Hash (keys, each, []=, default) gets Hash-of-nothing behavior and silently misbehaves; a plain object implementing [] would state the contract honestly and avoid the misleading 'this is a cached map' shape.

[BUG] The new FallbackLocaleList silently replaces the previous fallback target (I18n.default_locale, per the removed 'config.i18n.fallbacks = true' comment in production.rb) with a three-hop chain [user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en], changing the translation-resolution objective without the change being stated as the accepted intent. Any site whose SiteSetting.default_locale differs from I18n.default_locale now resolves missing keys against a different fallback chain than before the PR; e.g. with site default fr and I18n.default_locale en, a fr user previously got en strings only, and now also gets fr-first behavior — a behavioral change to every translation lookup smuggled in under a 'localization fallbacks' PR rather than explicitly accepted.

[BUG] The initializer applies fallbacks in every environment, whereas the removed config lines gated fallbacks to production/profile/cloud66 only, so development and test silently gain fallback behavior. The test suite now passes specs that previously failed on missing translations in non-default locales (missing keys fall back to :en instead of raising/returning the key), masking real translation gaps from CI — a constraint change (test strictness) that no reviewer explicitly accepted.

[BUG] set_locale unconditionally calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! which eager-loads the site default locale and :en on the request path, duplicating load logic that translate_accelerator already performs lazily and forcing up to two extra locale file loads per process on every request until warm. First requests after boot (or after any locale cache reset) do extra synchronous locale-file loading inside the per-request controller filter; the intent 'fallbacks ensure translations exist' is enforced at the wrong layer (every request instead of at lookup), coupling HTTP request handling to the accelerator's internal @loaded_locales bookkeeping.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! reads and mutates @loaded_locales without synchronization, the same unsynchronized-array pattern the neighboring translate method already uses, so concurrent first requests can both pass the include? check and load the same locale twice. Under concurrent cold-start traffic, duplicate load_locale work occurs per process; latent today because the existing code shares the pattern, but the next change that makes @loaded_locales stateful (e.g. unloading stale locales) inherits a data race that is now reachable from a request filter via ensure_loaded!.

[ADVISORY] Assigning a custom Hash subclass to I18n.fallbacks replaces I18n::Locale::Fallbacks wholesale, so any i18n-gem or Rails code that calls fallbacks methods beyond [] (e.g. []=, defaults computation) now hits Hash behavior or NoMethodError on a Hash that only overrides []. Future i18n gem upgrades or middleware that touches I18n.fallbacks with methods other than [] break in a way unrelated to this PR's stated intent; the TODO comment acknowledges the per-language extension is deferred but the override itself is the fragility, biting whoever upgrades the i18n gem next.

[BUG] The fallback chain is only warmed on the HTTP request path via set_locale, so any translation performed outside ApplicationController (mailers, background jobs, console tasks, serializers rendered in Sidekiq) falls back to locales that were never loaded into the accelerated backend. A background job or email rendering a missing key in the site/user locale hits I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, which probes the fallback locales (:en or site default) that the translate accelerator has not loaded (translate only load_locale(config.locale)); the lookup returns a 'translation missing' string in the rendered email/job output with no error raised or logged — the failure is silently embedded in user-facing content.

[ADVISORY] I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! now runs unguarded inside set_locale on every request, so a load failure for any locale in the chain (corrupt/missing custom locale YAML, unreadable file) raises before the controller can render, turning a localization misconfiguration into a site-wide 500 on every request. An operator who installs a broken custom locale (or the site default locale points at a locale with no loadable files) gets a hard 500 for all users instead of a degraded-but-working page in English; there is no rescue, no log-and-continue, and the error page itself depends on I18n that just failed to load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! runs on every request even when the accelerator's translate path would lazily load what is needed, and there is no test in the diff covering ensure_loaded! or the custom fallback ordering. Every request pays the fallback-chain computation and three include? checks; more importantly, the nontrivial new logic in FallbackLocaleList#[] (user-locale → site-locale → :en ordering, uniq/compact) has no spec, so a regression that reorders or drops the site-locale tier ships silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` inside `ApplicationController#set_locale`, which is typically executed per request, so the new fallback-chain computation and per-locale `include?`/load checks will run every request (via `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` and `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/behavior change rather than a correctness defect. Also, the PR introduces nontrivial new fallback ordering logic in `FallbackLocaleList#[]` (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) but the diff contains no accompanying specs to lock down ordering/tier behavior, making regressions in this new logic easier to ship silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash without ever calling super for [] or storing entries, faking a lookup table with an open method. Any I18n or plugin code that treats I18n.fallbacks as a real Hash (keys, each, []=, default) gets Hash-of-nothing behavior and silently misbehaves; a plain object implementing [] would state the contract honestly and avoid the misleading 'this is a cached map' shape.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` but overrides `[]` to compute an array and never populates the underlying Hash. As a result, Hash-API methods (`keys`, `each`, `[]=`, `default`, etc.) will reflect an empty hash while `[]` returns computed fallbacks, which is a misleading/fragile contract if any I18n or plugin code treats `I18n.fallbacks` as an actual lookup table. The diff itself doesn’t prove such downstream usage exists, so it’s a design/compatibility concern rather than a verified breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new FallbackLocaleList silently replaces the previous fallback target (I18n.default_locale, per the removed 'config.i18n.fallbacks = true' comment in production.rb) with a three-hop chain [user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en], changing the translation-resolution objective without the change being stated as the accepted intent. Any site whose SiteSetting.default_locale differs from I18n.default_locale now resolves missing keys against a different fallback chain than before the PR; e.g. with site default fr and I18n.default_locale en, a fr user previously got en strings only, and now also gets fr-first behavior — a behavioral change to every translation lookup smuggled in under a 'localization fallbacks' PR rather than explicitly accepted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from environment configs (which would have used Rails/I18n’s default fallback behavior based on `I18n.default_locale`) and replaces it with a custom `FallbackLocaleList` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` that hard-codes the fallback chain to `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change in translation resolution, especially when `SiteSetting.default_locale` differs from `I18n.default_locale`, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it is an incorrect/defective change (it may be intended).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The initializer applies fallbacks in every environment, whereas the removed config lines gated fallbacks to production/profile/cloud66 only, so development and test silently gain fallback behavior. The test suite now passes specs that previously failed on missing translations in non-default locales (missing keys fall back to :en instead of raising/returning the key), masking real translation gaps from CI — a constraint change (test strictness) that no reviewer explicitly accepted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production/profile/cloud66 environment configs and replaces it with a global initializer (`config/initializers/i18n.rb`) that unconditionally includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` (which falls back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`). Initializers run in all environments unless gated, so this does introduce fallback behavior in development/test as well. Whether that is a “bug” is not provable from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, environment-scope/CI-strictness behavioral change a reviewer may want to explicitly acknowledge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] set_locale unconditionally calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! which eager-loads the site default locale and :en on the request path, duplicating load logic that translate_accelerator already performs lazily and forcing up to two extra locale file loads per process on every request until warm. First requests after boot (or after any locale cache reset) do extra synchronous locale-file loading inside the per-request controller filter; the intent 'fallbacks ensure translations exist' is enforced at the wrong layer (every request instead of at lookup), coupling HTTP request handling to the accelerator's internal @loaded_locales bookkeeping.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` (in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`) iterates `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each, meaning default locale and `:en` can be loaded from within the per-request controller filter. Separately, `translate_accelerator` already tracks `@loaded_locales` and lazy-loads locales in `translate`, and now also has its own `ensure_loaded!(locale)` method. This makes the finding about duplicated/poorly layered locale-loading logic and request-path eager loading a valid, diff-grounded architectural/performance concern, but it’s not a clear functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! reads and mutates @loaded_locales without synchronization, the same unsynchronized-array pattern the neighboring translate method already uses, so concurrent first requests can both pass the include? check and load the same locale twice. Under concurrent cold-start traffic, duplicate load_locale work occurs per process; latent today because the existing code shares the pattern, but the next change that makes @loaded_locales stateful (e.g. unloading stale locales) inherits a data race that is now reachable from a request filter via ensure_loaded!.
matched_golden_ids: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes that @loaded_locales is read and mutated in ensure_loaded! without synchronization, leading to concurrent threads racing during first-load (duplicate loads/data race). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about lazy initialization and multi-threaded access without synchronization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Assigning a custom Hash subclass to I18n.fallbacks replaces I18n::Locale::Fallbacks wholesale, so any i18n-gem or Rails code that calls fallbacks methods beyond [] (e.g. []=, defaults computation) now hits Hash behavior or NoMethodError on a Hash that only overrides []. Future i18n gem upgrades or middleware that touches I18n.fallbacks with methods other than [] break in a way unrelated to this PR's stated intent; the TODO comment acknowledges the per-language extension is deferred but the override itself is the fragility, biting whoever upgrades the i18n gem next.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the default fallbacks object by doing `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, where `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` only customizes `[]` (and adds `ensure_loaded!`). This is a real compatibility/maintenance concern: code expecting the usual `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` semantics and APIs may now see plain-Hash behavior for other methods (e.g., `[]=`/defaults-related behavior), which is outside the PR’s stated intent of configuring fallback order. The diff itself doesn’t prove an immediate runtime failure, but it does introduce the fragility the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The fallback chain is only warmed on the HTTP request path via set_locale, so any translation performed outside ApplicationController (mailers, background jobs, console tasks, serializers rendered in Sidekiq) falls back to locales that were never loaded into the accelerated backend. A background job or email rendering a missing key in the site/user locale hits I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, which probes the fallback locales (:en or site default) that the translate accelerator has not loaded (translate only load_locale(config.locale)); the lookup returns a 'translation missing' string in the rendered email/job output with no error raised or logged — the failure is silently embedded in user-facing content.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom fallback list (config/initializers/i18n.rb) with an explicit `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` that loads the current locale + fallbacks via `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. But the only new callsite is `ApplicationController#set_locale` (`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`). The accelerated backend still only auto-loads `config.locale` in `translate` (`load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`), so fallback locales like `SiteSetting.default_locale` / `:en` are not guaranteed to be loaded unless `set_locale` ran. That makes fallbacks unreliable for code paths outside controllers (e.g., jobs/mailers), matching the finding’s core claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! now runs unguarded inside set_locale on every request, so a load failure for any locale in the chain (corrupt/missing custom locale YAML, unreadable file) raises before the controller can render, turning a localization misconfiguration into a site-wide 500 on every request. An operator who installs a broken custom locale (or the site default locale points at a locale with no loadable files) gets a hard 500 for all users instead of a degraded-but-working page in English; there is no rescue, no log-and-continue, and the error page itself depends on I18n that just failed to load.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call inside `ApplicationController#set_locale` (runs per request). The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` iterates the fallback chain and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!(l)` for each locale. The diff also introduces `I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale)` (in `translate_accelerator`) which calls `load_locale` unless already loaded, with no rescue/guard anywhere in `set_locale`. If `load_locale` raises on a missing/corrupt/unreadable locale file, that exception will bubble up and 500 the request before rendering. This is a newly introduced failure mode compared to merely enabling `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in env configs.
